item.title: Russia's war in Ukraine: the situation
item.description:
Russian sabotage cells damaged a Starlink centre in Lithuania and struck oil facilities in St Petersburg, while anti-Putin groups operated inside Russia. President Trump signed an executive order waiving a new Russia sanctions package, prompting Zelenskyy to accuse him of rewarding Putin. Ukraine used drones to evacuate and airlift a wounded soldier from the front line, a first-of-its-kind operation, and Russian drones killed children and an infant in a park in Kharkiv Oblast. 75,767 battle-related deaths occurred in 2024, according to UCDP.

item.title: Israel, Gaza and the West Bank: the situation
item.description:
Israeli police have detained ten settlers suspected of attacking a US photographer, a French mayor and other civilians in the West West Bank, torching cars and olive trees and wounding farmers. The World Food Programme is ending food aid for half a million people in Gaza because of funding shortfalls, while UNICEF reports that 340 children have been killed despite a ceasefire. Israel is resuming entry of private-sector goods into Gaza, where five people have been reported killed. The conflict has produced 21,440 battle-related deaths in 2024, according to UCDP.

item.title: Iran and the regional confrontation: the situation
item.description:
Iran has intensified its maritime campaign, attacking container ships in the Strait of Hormuz, striking a tug there, and launching missiles near the UAE while its IRGC conducts drone and artillery strikes in Iraqi Kurdistan after installing a new defence minister. Tehran has urged the reopening of the strait and Lavrov visited Tehran, publicly backing Iran amid questions about Moscow’s role. Houthi forces have repeatedly struck Yemeni army and government training camps, killing dozens of recruits in Shabwa and elsewhere. Pakistan has suspended border trade with Iran following cross-border violence. 123 battle-related deaths in 2024, according to UCDP.

item.description:

The surge of missile and ballistic strikes prompted Saudi Arabia to postpone the planned “Davos in the desert” summit and to send its skyscraper employees home due to heightened threats. These actions follow a series of recent Houthi attacks that have caused the highest single loss of life since the civil war resumed. The war produced 918 battle-related deaths in 2024, according to UCDP.

item.description:
Iraq is now coping with security gaps after the complete US troop withdrawal, while Baghdad and Tehran deepen cooperation by activating joint security committees and discussing stronger ties. Iraqi authorities are pursuing legal action against media incitement supporting pro-Iran armed groups, arresting a lawyer who brandished a gun in court and urging prosecutions, and the Kurdistan-based YBŞ is negotiating integration into state security forces. Heritage reconstruction continues in Nineveh and the Jordanian king has invited the Iraqi president for regional de-escalation talks. The conflict recorded 396 battle-related deaths in 2024, according to UCDP.

item.title: Sudan's civil war: the situation
item.description:
The Sudanese army and Rapid Support Forces are intensifying drone strikes on civilian sites, including a livestock market in Khartoum, a market where 80 people were killed, and gold-mining areas in West Kordofan and near the Egypt border, causing dozens of civilian deaths. Recent attacks have also hit a market in southern Sudan and an artisanal gold mine in South Kordofan, killing children and many civilians. These strikes expand the use of drones from combatant targets to economic and civilian locations, increasing civilian casualties. The conflict remains between the Sudanese Armed Forces and the Rapid Support Forces. 4,680 battle-related deaths in 2024, according to UCDP.

item.description:
Ethiopian forces have installed a caretaker administration in Tigray and are advancing toward the Eritrean border, while a pro-government militia says it has seized the regional airport and reports Eritrean forces suffered losses there. The United States, through Secretary of State Marco Rubio, is urging Ethiopia and Eritrea to de-escalate the fighting. Mekelle mayor Shishay Amare announced that elections will be held within six months and that Western Tigray will be settled through constitutional processes. The conflict caused 2,824 battle-related deaths in 2024, according to UCDP.

The Cockroach Janta party leader was arrested as a nationwide crackdown on protests expands. Bus attacks on routes bound for Kashmir occurred in Ludhiana, Haryana and Punjab, prompting condemnation from regional groups. item.description:

Zamfara experienced a false claim of an attack on the deputy governor and police rescued two abducted victims while recovering livestock. These incidents add to the ongoing bandit raids, ISWAP land-mine attacks and kidnappings previously reported. The conflict produced 1,486 battle-related deaths in 2024, according to UCDP.

Ethiopia announced the withdrawal of more than 3,000 troops from Somalia as its own conflict escalates, and Somaliland and Puntland were designated as "friendly" in an Israeli security framework. Somalia is screening travelers after Kenya confirmed an imported Ebola case and has agreed to acquire Pakistani JF‑17 fighter jets. item.description:
